extraFacts.fact: Wave 4 products are API certified and supplied with the API monogram by API-licensed manufacturers to the applicable specification: API 6A, API 16A, API 16C, API 16D or API 7K.

Sour gas service ratings on the Indus sour-service hammer union listings: Figure 1502 10,000 psi; Figure 1002 7,500 psi to 4" and 5,000 psi at 5" and 6"; Figure 1003 7,500 psi in 2" and 3" and 5,000 psi in 4" and 5"; Figure 1004 7,500 psi; Figure 602 6,000 psi; Figure 2202 15,000 psi, butt weld 2" to 6", is the sour-gas figure for 15,000 psi.
extraFacts.source: Indus Hydraulics Sour Gas Service Hammer Unions listings (/c/hammer-unions-sour-gas-service) and the guide /blog/hammer-union-figure-numbers (as-of 2026-10-06)

extraFacts.fact: Hammer unions of different figure numbers must never be joined. The male (thread) half of a 2" Figure 602 or Figure 1002 union will make up into the wing nut of a 2" Figure 1502, so a mismatched joint can look made up and then separate under pressure; IADC records a fatality from a 602-to-1502 mismatch and recommends teaching the differences between union types, go/no-go ring gauges, colour coding and segregated storage.
extraFacts.source: IADC Safety Alerts 06-01 'Mismatched Hammer Union Results in a Fatality' and 03-16 'Mismatched Hammer Unions Still Being Found' (iadc.org/safety-alerts)

extraFacts.fact: Accidents, including a fatality, have followed from hammering on hammer unions while the line was under pressure; bleed all pressure off a line before breaking it, and use lockout/tagout and permit-to-work on pressurised lines.

On elastomer-sealed hammer union figures the seal ring is a service item and should be replaced whenever it is cut, flattened or hardened. To order a union, give the figure, size, end connection and weld schedule, and whether the service is standard or sour.

faqs.q: What is a Figure 1002 butt weld sour gas hammer union used for?
faqs.a: A Figure 1002 sour gas butt weld hammer union is a low-alloy steel union with Sch XXS butt weld ends, supplied in H2S trim for cementing, acidizing, fracturing and choke lines. It is listed from 1" to 6" and is rated 7,500 psi (517 bar) falling with size.

faqs.q: How do I read the part number IH-HU-1002-BWXXS-SOUR-0300 on a sour Figure 1002 union?
faqs.a: IH-HU-1002-BWXXS-SOUR-0300 is a Figure 1002 union with Sch XXS butt weld ends, sour gas trim, 3" size. The last four digits give the size, from 0100 for 1" to 0600 for 6", and the size table lists each part number with its weight and dimensions.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure of the sour Figure 1002 butt weld hammer union by size?
faqs.a: The sour Figure 1002 butt weld union is rated 7,500 psi (517 bar) cold working pressure at 1", 2", 3" and 4", and 5,000 psi (345 bar) at 5" and 6". The 1" to 4" sizes are tested at 12,000 psi. Read the rating for your size in the table, not from the figure number.

faqs.q: What sizes does the sour Figure 1002 butt weld union come in?
faqs.a: It is listed in 1", 2", 3", 4", 5" and 6" with Sch XXS butt weld ends, weighing from 1,800 g at 1" to 39,000 g at 6". For line pipe threaded ends see the [sour Figure 1002 threaded union](/p/figure-1002-hammer-union-threaded-sour-gas-service-7500-psi), which covers 1" to 4".

faqs.q: Should I choose the sour Figure 1002 or Figure 1004 at 5" or 6"?
faqs.a: At 5" and 6" the sour Figure 1002 is rated 5,000 psi and seals on an O-ring, while the [sour Figure 1004 butt weld union](/p/figure-1004-hammer-union-butt-weld-sour-gas-service-7500-psi) is rated 7,500 psi with a lip-type seal. Choose the 1004 if you need the higher rating or want to avoid making an O-ring union up perfectly square.

faqs.q: What seal and material does the sour Figure 1002 butt weld union use?
faqs.a: It is low-alloy steel with a replaceable elastomer seal ring, lip type from 1" to 4" and O-ring at 5" and 6". The seal is made by the seat and ring, not the thread, so a leaking union usually needs a new seal ring or sub.

faqs.q: Can I use a standard Figure 1002 union in H2S service?
faqs.a: No, use the sour gas trim for H2S service; the standard service Figure 1002 is not the sour version. Confirm the service class, the trim and the certification you need on the enquiry.

faqs.q: Which unions will mate with a sour Figure 1002 butt weld hammer union?
faqs.a: A Figure 1002 mates only with another Figure 1002 of the same size. Never join it to a different figure: industry safety alerts record that a 2" Figure 602 or 1002 male half can make up into a 2" Figure 1502 wing nut and separate under pressure, so segregate and mark the unions.

faqs.q: How is a sour Figure 1002 butt weld union made up and serviced?
faqs.a: A Figure 1002 is made up by striking the wing nut lugs with a hammer until the subs seat on the seal. Bleed the line to zero before breaking it out, never hammer on a pressurised union, and replace the seal ring whenever it is cut, flattened or hardened.

faqs.q: How does the sour Figure 1002 differ from the standard service version?
faqs.a: The sour Figure 1002 is supplied in H2S trim and is rated 7,500 psi to 4", below the standard service union of the same figure. See the [standard service Figure 1002](/p/hammer-union-set-1002-series-npt-npt-10-000-psi-standard-service) if the line carries no H2S, and read the sizes table for each rating.
